newsitem.title: LATVIA: RULES FOR UNIBANKA FOREIGN PLACEMENT SET.
newsitem.headline: RULES FOR UNIBANKA FOREIGN PLACEMENT SET.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) on Friday said it has set the rules for the sale of the state's stake in Unibanka and the arrangements to find a financial company to place the shares abroad.

"The LPA decided to place abroad no less than 5.8 million Unibanka shares of the 8.3 million state stake, the latter being the figure after the latest capital boost through the bonus share issue," Uldis Kalninsh, an LPA official, told Reuters.
"The application deadline for international financial intermediaries interested in arranging the placement is June 30," he added.
The agency also plans to sell a part of its stake locally and will decide separately on the size and form of the sale.
The tender will be arranged by Coopers & Lybrand and invitations will be sent out to some 30 companies.
The candidates for the final tender will be chosen on July 14 and the arranger will be named on August 11, Kalninsh said.
The local placement may be a cash auction or sale in separate quotas through a brokearage. The LPA has earlier said that it would like to sell locally some 10 percent of its stake.
According to current shareholder agreements with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the state's stake should not fall below ten percent while the EBRD is a shareholder.
"We are currently in talks with the EBRD on a possibility of a total selloff of the state stake," Kalninsh said.
He also said that among financial companies interested in placing the shares were Nomura, Union Bank of Switzerland, Bank of New York, Daiwa Securities and Hansa Investments.
